headline: Slow-grind decade: frontier defaults, a shallow 2029 stall, and walls growing higher

events: Fed and ECB trim rates once each to ~3.25%/2% as inflation sticks near 3%; long yields stay elevated on term-premium worries
US extends sectoral tariffs to pharmaceuticals and chips equipment; EU responds with targeted steel and EV safeguards
Ukraine front freezes into a de facto armistice-without-treaty; Red Sea shipping still partially diverted
Ethiopia and Malawi restructurings drag on; Pakistan rolls over IMF programme under strain
AI capex keeps rising but enterprise adoption grows slowly (~15% of firms); first wave of back-office hiring freezes in banking and insurance
US election year brings populist fiscal promises; deficit stays ~7% of GDP
Japan 10-year JGB yields touch 2.3%, BoJ slows balance-sheet runoff to calm markets
Bolivia defaults and Egypt needs an emergency IMF augmentation as Gulf support thins
China's growth slips to ~3.8%; Beijing pushes export volumes into the Global South, prompting anti-dumping cases from Brazil, Mexico, India and Turkey
Record heat summer in South Asia; wheat export curbs from India lift food inflation briefly
AI-infrastructure spending plateaus after disappointing monetisation; tech equities fall ~25%, triggering a shallow global slowdown (world growth ~2.1%)
Central banks cut to ~2.75%, but sticky services inflation limits easing; G20 inflation averages ~3%
Border clashes between Ethiopia and Eritrea escalate into a sustained regional war drawing in Gulf patrons
Sri Lanka and Kenya hit renewed debt distress; G20 Common Framework criticised as dead letter
Sporadic cost-of-living protests across Latin America and Southern Europe; youth unemployment in North Africa above 30%
Modest recovery; AI tools cheaper and diffusing into mid-sized firms (~25% adoption), mainly in customer service, coding and logistics
US-China sign a narrow 'managed trade' truce on soybeans and rare earths but tech export controls widen
NDC 2035 updates fall well short; COP35 marked by walkouts over adaptation finance
UK and France face bond-market jitters during budget rounds, forcing small austerity packages
Renewables surpass 40% of global electricity in some months; coal use in India still rising
Global growth ~2.7%; debt at ~103% of world GDP with interest costs crowding out investment in many budgets
US debt passes 130% of GDP; Treasury lengthens bill-heavy issuance and a bipartisan fiscal commission is announced with little teeth
EU agrees incremental capital-markets and defence-bond reforms rather than a big fiscal union step
Warming 5-year average crosses ~1.55C; insurance withdrawal from coastal Florida and parts of southern Europe accelerates
Trust indices hit new lows as voters see stagnating real wages and stalled housing reforms

winners: India and Vietnam as connector economies capturing diverted manufacturing
Large AI platform and cloud incumbents with pricing power after the 2029 shakeout
Gulf states and defence contractors benefiting from bloc rivalry and arms demand
losers: Frontier-market debtors in Africa and South Asia squeezed by high rates and aid cuts
Young renters in Western cities facing unaffordable housing
Mid-skill clerical workers in advanced economies
Small export-dependent economies caught between US and Chinese rules
bullets: The world never crashed but never recovered momentum: growth averaged ~2.6%, below the pre-2020 trend.
Public debt crept to ~103% of world GDP; interest bills now rival defence and education in many budgets.
Five sovereign debt crises, all in lower-income countries, resolved slowly and partially through ad hoc deals.
Tariff walls rose a notch further; trade runs through 'connector' countries and regional supply chains.
AI reached about three in ten firms, shaving clerical and support jobs more than creating headline mass unemployment.
A brief 2029 AI-capex correction exposed concentration risk but central banks cushioned it.
Climate policy lagged badly: emissions only plateaued, warming approaches 1.6C, and adaptation gaps widened.
Polarisation and low trust froze big reforms; politics oscillates between populist spending promises and bond-market discipline.
wildcard: An Ethiopia-Eritrea war in 2029 that drew in Gulf patrons and disrupted Red Sea shipping a second time.
image_description: In a hot, crowded Nairobi minibus in 2031, a young graduate scrolls AI-generated gig listings on a cracked phone while a solar-powered billboard outside flashes a government notice about yet another fuel-price hike.
